title: See Where the Great Incarnate God
description: See Where the Great Incarnate God in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 45, headed “The last judgment, Rev. 21. 5-8”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: See where the great in-car-nate God Fills a ma-jes-tic throne, While from the skies his aw-ful voice Bears the last judg-ment down.

lines: See where the great incarnate God
While from the skies his awful voice
"I am the first, and I the last,
"Such favours as a God can give
"Ye thirsty souls come taste the streams
"The saint that triumphs o'er his sins,
"They shall be taken from my sight,
O may I stand before the Lamb,
When earth and seas are fled!
And hear the Judge pronounce my name
May I with those for ever dwell
While sinners banish'd down to hell,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
